key_insight: Internally stirred active particles and a deformable elastic vesicle co-evolve: activity reorganizes the membrane, while membrane softness and anchoring reshape the collective flow, producing distinct shape-and-dynamics transitions as activity increases.
engineering_relevance: This work informs the design of soft, active microcontainers and synthetic cells by showing how boundary mechanics can tune mixing, transport, and flow states in confined active suspensions.
method: 2D weakly extensible elastic-ring model with bending rigidity in Stokes flow
Kinetic theory for a dilute extensile active-particle suspension coupled to the vesicle by hydrodynamic and alignment interactions
Stability analysis plus nonlinear volume-conserving immersed-boundary simulations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical stability thresholds and simulation results that identify successive morphodynamic states: spindle, rotor, fluctuating spinner, and turbulent self-stirring behavior.
watch_item: The study is a 2D model with weak-anchoring assumptions and dilute suspension kinetics, so quantitative behavior may change for 3D vesicles, stronger coupling, or denser active matter.
paper_title: Active Sculpting: morphodynamics of internally stirred active vesicles
